description.value: Cross-sectional task-based fMRI study examining visuospatial dysfunction and brain activation in female patients with rheumatoid arthritis, including relationships between left precuneus activation, mental rotation performance, and disease activity.

spans.text: To identify the potential diagnostic biomarkers of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and assess the relation between visuospatial dysfunction and disease activity in RA patients using mental rotation task (MRT)-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of rheumatoid arthritis patients and matched healthy controls; RA patients were further classified as active or in remission according to DAS28.

spans.text: In this cross-sectional study, 29 female patients with RA were recruited from the Department of Rheumatology, the First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, during the period of December 2019 to April 2021.
The neuropsychological scales were evaluated by two psychologists, and the HAQ and DAS28 were completed by two rheumatologists.

The mental rotation task (MRT) is a well-known task for assessing visuospatial function, which involves the ability to mentally transform three-dimensional objects in space [ 12 ].

description.value: Block-designed mental rotation task using three-dimensional graphics, with comparison and rotation blocks presented during fMRI.

spans.text: The block-designed MRT was programmed and presented using E-Prime 3.0 software (Psychology Software Tools Inc; PST, Pittsburgh, PA, USA).

instructions.value: Participants compared paired three-dimensional drawings and pressed the left button when drawings were identical and the right button otherwise.

spans.text: If the two drawings were identical, participants were required to press the left button, otherwise the right button was pressed.

stimuli.value: Three-dimensional graphics designed by Shepard and Metzler.

spans.text: The 3D graphics, designed by Shepard and Metzler [ 11 ], were presented to participants during the fMRI scan.
If the two drawings were identical, participants were required to press the left button, otherwise the right button was pressed.
MRT was performed synchronously during the MRI scan, and the accuracy and response time were recorded by E-prime.
There were two types of tasks: comparison and rotation.

description.value: Two drawings were presented in the same plane with no rotation angle.

spans.text: In the comparison task, two drawings were in the same plane with no rotation angle.
There were two types of tasks: comparison and rotation.

description.value: Two drawings were presented on different planes at a 100° rotation angle and participants judged whether they were identical after mental rotation.

spans.text: In the rotation block, a picture had two 3D drawings that were not on the same plane and were placed at a certain rotation angle (100°).
